title: The closed point lies over the distinguished point
statement: Let S be a scheme, Ω an algebraically closed field, s : Spec Ω → S a geometric point, A a commutative local ring, and e : Spec A ≅ S_(s), where S_(s) is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and its structural map ρ_s is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Then ρ_s(e(closedPoint A)) = s(closedPoint Ω).

proof.text: Equip Ω with the algebra structure given by the geometric-point residue map; the required compatibility is reflexivity. Apply the unchanged upstream AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationResidue, the residue clause of the functoriality node in the full strict-localization presentation, to obtain a local-ring structure on C = strictHenselization s and the structural-image equation for closedPoint C.

Every point of a local spectrum specializes to its closed point. Apply this in C to e(closedPoint A), and in A to e.inv(closedPoint C); map the latter specialization by e.hom. The inverse identity and T0 separation give e(closedPoint A)=closedPoint C. Substitute into the structural-image equation.

lean.statement:
theorem strictHenselizationStructuralMap_closedPoint_eq
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω A : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (e : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictLocalization s) :
    (e.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase s) (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) =
      s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)
